title: Temporal dynamics, functional constraints, and abundance shape buzz-pollination networks in a tropical savanna
content:
Abstract
Buzz-pollinated plants possess specialized floral structures that require vibratory pollen extraction, strongly shaping plant–pollinator interactions. In a Brazilian savanna community, we investigated how flowering phenology and bee functional traits (body size, sociality, and buzzing behaviour) influence the structure and dynamics of bee–flower interaction networks across species of Fabaceae, Melastomataceae, and Bixaceae. We monitored five poricidal-flowered species over one year and classified bees into functional groups based on buzzing behaviour. Flowering was highly seasonal, following a sequential pattern that probably ensures temporal continuity of floral resources. Despite this strong seasonality, bee richness remained stable across seasons, suggesting temporal tracking of floral resources by pollinators. Network analyses revealed that bees capable of vibrating entire flowers formed more specialized interaction patterns, whereas non-vibrating bees exhibited more generalist and less structured interactions. Individual specialization was not explained by body size or sociality, but centrality increased strongly with species abundance, indicating that frequent visitors play a disproportionate role in maintaining network connectivity. Together, our findings show that buzz-pollination networks are structured by the interplay of temporal dynamics, functional constraints, and species abundance, highlighting their potential sensitivity to environmental change.
